correctness.rationale: Verifier verify_cores.py passes (VERIFY_OK) from artifacts. Auditor independently re-checked every listed core: beta(partition)==beta, partition(beta)==partition, size(beta)==sum(partition)==listed size, Durfee recomputed matches, every hook multiset contains no multiple of the triple, and every beta-set is s,t,u-flush. Headline hook multisets hand-checked: hooks([4,1,1])=hooks([3,1,1,1])=[1,1,2,2,3,6]; hooks([6,2,2,2])=hooks([4,4,1,1,1,1])=[1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3,4,4,8,9], all free of {4,5,7} resp. {5,6,7} multiples. Completeness established by two independent routes: (i) fresh triple-flush DFS over [1,st-1] (code distinct from verifier) yields exactly the 10 and 21 census beta-sets, and pair DFS yields Anderson 14 and 42; (ii) exhaustive partition hook-scan to the classical pair max-size bounds (4,5): (16-1)(25-1)/24=15 and (5,6): (25-1)(36-1)/24=35 finds exactly the same 10 and 21 partitions. Hence any triple-core is a pair-core bounded by those sizes, so the scan is complete independently of the abacus bound prose. Flush<->hook equivalence machine-checked on all 272 partitions to size 12. Size histograms sum to counts; claimed gaps (no size 5 or >=7 for (4,5,7); no 7,10,11 or >=13 for (5,6,7)) follow from exhaustive lists. The DRAFT bound prose (B subset [1,st-1]) is informal but its conclusion is corroborated by the agreeing pair-size scan and Anderson cross-check; beta-flush lemma is classical (Anderson/James) and additionally machine-checked on the needed range. No computation error or boundary omission (empty core included, vacuous conditions hold).

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison to nearest priors, not timestamp logic. Anderson (2002) gives only pair counts (4,5)=14, (5,6)=42, used as cross-check. Yang-Zhong-Zhou (2014) proves count/max/average formulas for interval (s,s+1,s+2)-cores: for s=5 this implies count 21 (1+10+10) and max size 12, and Xiong (2014) implies 1-or-2 maximizers by parity (2 for odd s=5). DRAFT explicitly does NOT claim those aggregates as new; novelty is scoped to full size distributions, Durfee data, every beta-set, and explicit witness partitions, which no formula implies and which were verified absent from those papers' abstracts/full text (aggregate-only). (4,5,7) is non-interval and outside YZZ/Xiong/Yan-Yu-Zhou interval theorems entirely, so even its count 10 is not implied. Baek-Nam-Yu (2017) gives a counting expression for (b1..bn)-cores with a coprime pair and self-conjugate interval maxima — counts in principle, not distributions/betas/witnesses. Yan-Yu-Zhou (2019) counts interval (s,..,s+k) via Dyck paths, not non-interval triples and not distributions. Li-Sha-Xiong (2024) proves limit laws motivating exact data but no finite triple census. Live abstract fetches confirm aggregate-only scope. No source was found recording these histograms, Durfee tables, beta lists, or named maximizers; distributions are not mechanically derivable from max/count/average without enumeration.

value.rationale: Strongest headline is a complete, replayable census for two natural finite coprime triple families with full size histograms, Durfee data, every beta-set, and named largest-size witnesses — an eligible census/witness finding form. Objects motivated before computation (Anderson enumeration, Armstrong-Johnson size theorem, Olsson-Stanton/multicore stability, rational Catalan, Hecke blocks, Ehrhart-type size-distribution programs; Li-Sha-Xiong limit laws create demand for exact finite distributions). Values were not known or mechanically implied (distributions, Durfee, beta identities, witness partitions; only (5,6,7) count/max/m maximizer-count aggregates were implied and are honestly scoped as prior). A future researcher testing stability/rational-Catalan/block conjectures could reasonably need these precise beta-sets, gaps (e.g. missing size 5; missing 7,10,11), and extremal witnesses. Not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny benchmark tweak, or unexplained enumeration: exact invariant tables with hook-check certificates over motivated scopes. Both families are complete (not an incomplete census); no general criterion or downstream theorem is demanded.

Aggregate formulas only; for s=5 implies count 21 and max 12 but does not tabulate size distribution, Durfee data, beta-sets, or witness partitions.

residual_risks: (5,6,7) aggregate count 21, max value 12, and two-maximizer count are implied by YZZ/Xiong formulas; only distributions, Durfee, beta-sets, and named witnesses are new — DRAFT scopes this correctly but a careless citation could overclaim the bare numbers.

Finiteness-bound prose in DRAFT is informal; completeness relies on classical Anderson/poset theory plus replayable code and the auditor's independent pair-size scan — rerun requires executing the stdlib verifier.
